findings.bible: Section 2 DEVICES/SENSORS fact 14 "Compass heading math (exact)": flat heading = fmod(atan2(2(xy-zw), 1-2(x^2+z^2))*180/pi + 360, 360); upright = atan2(2(xz+yw), 2(yz-xw)); mode selection |gZ| < cos45 && gY < -cos45.
findings.target: modules/devices/include/Microsoft/Devices/Sensors/Detail/AndroidCompassMath.hpp::ConvertRotationVectorToMagneticHeadingDegrees (atan2(R01, R11) with R01 = 2(xy - zw), R11 = 1 - 2(x^2 + z^2)) and ::ConvertRotationVectorToUprightMagneticHeadingDegrees (atan2(R02, R12) with R02 = 2(xz + yw), R12 = 2(yz - xw)); both finish with fmod(degrees + 360, 360). Read; not executed.
findings.site_now: deep-dives/services/sensors-and-vibration.html#compass gives the pose test and the two gravity components but says only "then uses the upright or flat azimuth formula"; neither azimuth formula appears anywhere on the site (searched atan2(2, xy - zw).

fix.old_html: then uses the upright or flat azimuth formula; results are normalized to [0°, 360°).
fix.html: then uses the upright or flat azimuth formula: flat (device lying face-up) is atan2(2(xy − zw), 1 − 2(x² + z²)) and upright is atan2(2(xz + yw), 2(yz − xw)), the R01/R11 and R02/R12 entries of the quaternion's rotation matrix; results are normalized to [0°, 360°). findings.bible: Section 3 AUDIO fact 23: XACT is a hand-written parser; .xgs magic 0x46534758 ("XGSF"), contentVersion 46 expected else a stderr warning; .xwb magic 0x444E4257 ("WBND"), version > 46 warns; .xsb sound/cue flags COMPLEX 0x01, HAS_RPC 0x02, HAS_TRACK_RPC 0x04, RPC_MASK 0x0E, HAS_DSP 0x10, CUE_SINGLE_SOUND 0x04.
findings.target: modules/audio/src/Internal/XactParser.cpp::ParseXgs accepts magic 0x46534758 (bytes "XGSF") and the byte-swapped 0x58475346 ("FSGX"); the P9-AUDIT-003 comment says the big-endian magic is cosmetic because every later field is read in host order by Ctx::u16/u32/f32 with no byte-swapping, so a genuinely big-endian file passes the magic check and is then misparsed; ::ReadXwbSegmentTable accepts only 0x444E4257 ("WBND") and throws "XWB: invalid magic"; ParseXsb accepts 0x4B424453 ("SDBK") and the swapped 0x5344424B with the same caveat. Read; not executed.
findings.site_now: deep-dives/services/xact-runtime.html#loading gives the version-46 rule and the warning but no magic values, no accepted-magic or byte-order rule; searched XGSF, WBND, SDBK, FSGX, big-endian near XACT: absent from the whole site.

fix.html: Each format is recognized by a four-byte magic at the start of the file: XGSF for the .xgs settings file, SDBK for the .xsb sound bank and WBND for the .xwb wave bank; any other magic is rejected. The .xgs and .xsb checks also accept the byte-swapped spelling (FSGX, KBDS) used by big-endian console builds, but the parser reads every later field in host byte order, so a genuinely big-endian file passes the magic check and is then misparsed instead of being rejected (the source comment calls the acceptance cosmetic); the wave bank check accepts only the little-endian form. Treat files from the Windows toolchain as the supported input. Read from XactParser.cpp at 009d40f5; not executed.

findings.bible: Section 1 INPUT fact 13: the button flags are derived from the *processed* thumbstick by comparing against deadZoneSize on each axis (GamePadState.cpp). (At TARGET these are the eight thumbstick-direction Buttons, not GamePadDPad.)
findings.target: modules/input/src/Xna/GamePadState.cpp::GamePadState(GamePadThumbSticks, GamePadTriggers, GamePadButtons, GamePadDPad) calls StickToButtons(stick, ..., GamePad::LeftDeadZone / RightDeadZone): a direction button is set when the already processed stick component is > +dz or < -dz on that axis (strict comparison); LeftTrigger/RightTrigger when the trigger is > GamePad::TriggerThreshold. GamePad::ExcludeAxisDeadZone rescales as (|v| - dz) / (1 - dz).
findings.site_now: deep-dives/services/gamepads-and-haptics.html#deadzones says only "the eight thumbstick-direction buttons from the dead-zoned sticks"; the threshold (the same constants applied a second time to the processed value) is not stated (searched StickToButtons, ThumbstickLeft: absent).

fix.old_html: and the eight thumbstick-direction buttons from the dead-zoned sticks.
fix.html: and the eight thumbstick-direction buttons (LeftThumbstickLeft to RightThumbstickDown) when the already dead-zoned stick value on that axis lies beyond LeftDeadZone or RightDeadZone (StickToButtons in GamePadState.cpp). That is a second threshold applied on top of the mode's own dead zone: with IndependentAxes a direction button needs a raw deflection of about 0.42 on the left stick and 0.46 on the right, not 0.24 and 0.27 (arithmetic over the source, not measured).

findings.bible: Section 5 NET fact 26: NetworkSessionJoinError has exactly three values: SessionNotFound, SessionNotJoinable, SessionFull.
findings.target: modules/net/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Net/NetworkSessionJoinError.hpp (three enumerators); modules/net/src/Xna/NetworkSession.cpp EndJoin throws NetworkSessionJoinException(..., SessionNotFound) after the 5 s wait, and the catch-all path uses the (message, cause) constructor whose joinError_ defaults to SessionNotFound; a search of modules/net/src, modules/net/include and modules/c-api/src finds no throw site for SessionNotJoinable or SessionFull (only tests and C API ordinal static_asserts). Read; not executed.
findings.site_now: deep-dives/services/network-sessions.html#join and #limits name SessionNotFound (timeout) and SessionFull (never raised, CNA-BUG-267); SessionNotJoinable and the fact that only one of the three values is ever produced are absent (searched SessionNotJoinable: no page).

fix.html: NetworkSessionJoinError declares three values, SessionNotFound, SessionNotJoinable and SessionFull, and only the first is ever produced at this snapshot: it is what EndJoin reports when the handshake does not complete, and the default of NetworkSessionJoinException, which the catch-all path also uses. SessionFull is never raised (CNA-BUG-267) and SessionNotJoinable has no producer at all, so a refused join (a host that is playing with AllowJoinInProgress false disconnects the hello) cannot be told from an absent host by the error value. Read from the sources at 009d40f5; not executed.

findings.bible: Section 1 sharp-runtime FACT 11: Prop.hpp is a pure macro header; six public macros in declare/implement pairs (DDATA/IDATA, DGETTER/IGETTER, DGETTERSTATIC/IGETTERSTATIC); generated shape: backing field name_, [[nodiscard]] getNameProperty() returning const T&, setNameProperty in const-ref and rvalue-ref overloads; underneath a token-pasting kit.
findings.target: sharp-runtime 41b918c9 modules/core/include/SharpRuntime/Prop.hpp: DEF_PROP(type, name, getter, setter, member, static_keyword, const_return_qualifier, ref_return_qualifier, const_method_qualifier) declares an optional private field name_, a [[nodiscard]] get<Name>Property() and set<Name>Property(const type&) / (type&&); DDATA = getter+setter+member, DGETTER = getter+member, DGETTERSTATIC = static getter; IMPL_PROP and IDATA/IGETTER/IGETTERSTATIC define the bodies. CNA 009d40f5 modules/graphics/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Graphics/Viewport.hpp declares six properties with DEF_PROP(..., member0, ...) next to its own X_ etc. fields, and modules/graphics/src/Xna/Viewport.cpp defines them with IMPL_PROP(..., Viewport, nothing). Read; not compiled.
findings.site_now: deep-dives/sharp-runtime/components-and-consumption.html#global-macros names DEF_PROP, DDATA, DGETTER, IDATA and IGETTER and says Prop.hpp defines 31 names and that CNA headers use DEF_PROP, but never says what the generators declare (field, accessor and setter shapes, the on/off flag arguments, the declare/implement split); searched DDATA, DEF_PROP, getNameProperty shape: absent elsewhere.

fix.html: What the property macros generate. DEF_PROP(type, name, getter, setter, member, static, const-return, ref-return, const-method) declares, inside the class it is written in, an optional private backing field name_, a [[nodiscard]] accessor getNameProperty() and two setters, setNameProperty(const type&) and setNameProperty(type&&); the getter1/getter0, setter1/setter0 and member1/member0 arguments switch each piece on or off. DDATA (field, getter and setter), DGETTER (field and getter) and DGETTERSTATIC (a static getter) are presets of it, and IDATA, IGETTER and IGETTERSTATIC are their counterparts for the .cpp file, which define the accessor bodies; IMPL_PROP is the low-level form. CNA's Viewport.hpp uses the low-level form with member0: the class keeps its own X_, Y_ and similar fields, the header declares the accessors, and Viewport.cpp defines them with IMPL_PROP. Read from Prop.hpp at 41b918c9 and CNA at 009d40f5; not compiled.

findings.target: scripts/htmldom-browser-test.mjs: near(..., 12) for the smoke inside/outside pixels, near(..., 25) for the atlas interior sample(12, 21) and near-edge sample(39, 21), TIMEOUT_MS = CNA_HTMLDOM_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS ?? 60000, sample() offsets by document.getElementById("cna-dom-root").getBoundingClientRect(); scripts/svgdom-browser-test.mjs: isColor(..., 20) at four scissor-order points. findings.site_now: deep-dives/platforms/web-build-and-main-loop.html#htmldom says the driver reads points with getImageData (inside and outside a scissor rectangle, an atlas interior and a point near its edge) but gives no tolerances, no sample geometry and no timeout variable; #svgdom likewise; searched 12, 25, 20 tolerance, CNA_HTMLDOM_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS: absent.

fix.html: The compositor checks use bounded per-channel tolerances rather than exact matches. In the smoke page the point at logical (70,70), inside both the sprite and the scissor rectangle, must be within 12 of pure red on each channel and the point at (90,90), outside it, within 12 of the CornflowerBlue clear colour (100, 149, 237); in the pixel page the atlas interior at (12,21) and the point two pixels inside the drawn region's right edge at (39,21) must both be within 25 of pure red. Sample points are offset by the bounding rectangle of #cna-dom-root, and the wait for the page's verdict is bounded by CNA_HTMLDOM_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS (default 60000). The edge check is deliberately as tight as the interior one because the DOM path is expected to show no bleed at that point, unlike the Canvas 2D path (see Targets and readback). The SVG_DOM driver applies the same style of bound, 20 per channel, at its four scissor-order points. Read from htmldom-browser-test.mjs and svgdom-browser-test.mjs at 009d40f5; not executed.

findings.bible: Section E FACT 44: the atlas near-edge pixel test uses tolerance 25, "deliberately tight because the DOM path must not bleed" (the reason: HTML_DOM has two draw paths that differ at atlas edges under linear filtering).
findings.target: docs/html-dom-renderer.md known limitation 14 (HTMLDOM-119): the Canvas2D render-target path bleeds the adjacent undrawn atlas texel into an edge sample inside the drawn source rectangle under linear filtering at a large fractional scale (measured (147,0,108) against a hand-derived (154,0,101)), while the DOM <div> background-image path, a hard clip by CSS, measures zero bleed; not fixed; modules/renderers/html-dom/examples/htmldom_pixel_verification_test.cpp (HTMLDOM-119) checks both paths; scripts/htmldom-browser-test.mjs comment at the near-edge assertion. Read; not executed.
findings.site_now: deep-dives/renderers/browser-dom-renderers.html#html-dom-targets explains that a bound RenderTarget2D is an off-screen Canvas 2D context and lists one accepted readback gap, but not that the two paths differ at atlas edges under linear filtering; searched bleed, background-image, atlas near HTML_DOM: absent.

fix.html: The two draw paths do not agree at atlas edges under linear filtering. Draw an in-bounds source rectangle from a larger, unpadded atlas at a large fractional scale: the Canvas 2D path, which is the one active while a RenderTarget2D is bound, blends the adjacent, undrawn atlas texel into a sample that lies inside the drawn rectangle, which is what real hardware sampling an unpadded atlas also does; the CSS background-image path, whose element box is a hard clip, shows no bleed at the same point. CNA's own limitations list records this as a measured divergence between the renderer's two paths and leaves it unfixed, and the browser pixel check for the DOM path is kept tight because of it.
